breadcrumb: 01. University of Oregon Institute for Policy Research & Engagement
tldr: The University of Oregon Institute for Policy Research & Engagement advocates for treating economic development as a core Oregon state priority with a coordinated statewide strategy. Despite ranking 9th nationally in innovation, Oregon's decentralized ecosystem has failed to retain businesses—68% of those targeted by out-of-state recruiters relocate or expand elsewhere. The authors propose adapting organizational models from Pennsylvania, New York, Michigan, Colorado, and Kentucky to strengthen coordination and outcomes.

bullets.text: 68% of Oregon businesses contacted by out-of-state economic development entities ultimately chose to relocate or expand outside Oregon (IPRE Business Recruitment Report, 2024)
Oregon ranked 9th nationally for innovation but 28th for overall economic strength and 48th for business friendliness in CNBC 2024 rankings
Oregon ranked 43rd out of 50 in Chief Executive 2024 rankings and 49th in corporate tax environment (Tax Foundation 2025)
Nearly one quarter of Oregon's workforce is over age 55, raising concerns about imminent loss of institutional knowledge and critical skillsets
One in eight Oregon jobs connected to international trade as of 2023, showing state's position in global supply chains
Oregon ranks near bottom among peers in per capita economic development spending when infrastructure is excluded (Council for Community and Economic Research)
Identifies push factors driving business departure: regulatory complexity, tax burden, lack of industrial land, high housing costs, and workforce gaps

Proposes examining five states' economic development structures: Pennsylvania (strong executive leadership), New York (regional approaches), Michigan (public-private partnerships), Colorado (high-tech plus rural), Kentucky (rural focus)
